title: WarrantRequirement
description: PROPOSED, NOT ADMITTED. Declares whether an admitted control requires a logical warrant, and if so under which kernel profile and at which minimum assurance grade. There is NO implicit or default mode: a control must state its requirement explicitly, because a defaulted warrant requirement is indistinguishable from one nobody thought about. This object is a separate dimension from `decision_mode`; see adr/ADR-013.md.

mode.description: `required`: the control's decision depends on a logical warrant. `not_required`: the control has a logical component but does not gate on a warrant. `not_applicable`: the control contains no logical-warrant requirement at all. NOTE: `not_required` is NOT permission to skip authority, admission, evidence, or version checks. Those are independent of this object and are never waived by it.

kernel_profile_id.description: Identifies the kernel semantics AND the disposition/grade vocabulary the control was admitted against, for example `ztl-v0.1`. Required when mode is `required`. A warrant produced under a different profile is MISBOUND and cannot ALLOW: grades and dispositions are not portable between kernels, and comparing them across profiles would silently equate different guarantees.

minimum_warranty_grade.description: Least durable warranty grade this control accepts. `hereditary` accepts only results invariant under every admissible monotone refinement. `sound` additionally accepts results that never lie about the present marking but may stall. Setting `sound` is an explicit institutional decision to tolerate a non-monotone warrant; it must never be a default. Required when mode is `required`.

on_insufficient_grade.description: What the runtime does when the observed grade is below the minimum. The outcome is always recorded with decision_basis CONTROL_REQUIREMENT: the grounds did establish the claim, and the control declined to act on that grade. It is neither a defect nor a doubt about the logic. Required when mode is `required`.

unverified_ground_policy.description: Whether this control may act on a positive result that depends on unverified grounds, and how. `forbid`: never act on conditional support. `escalate`: route to a human. `allow_with_disclosure`: permitted to proceed, with the missing grounds preserved on the decision record. Required and non-null when mode is `required`. A minimum warranty grade alone is NOT sufficient authorisation to act on unverified grounds: the grade says how durable the result is, this field says whether the institution accepts a result that rides an unverified link. They are different questions and a control must answer both.
